39: strategy/A115 {NORMAL}; the five trims released and
Fault injected: the vane is frozen at 0.15.
The residual is keyed to one command: for cmd-31 the
observer predicts the fall that opening 0.15 -> 1.00
owes us. The published r = measured - predicted; the
CUSUM accumulates measured - ceiling, which coincides
with it in a room at design occupancy — the case
drawn here. S = max(0, S + r - 30).
S passes the suspicion threshold 0.6 h = 90 ppm, so a case
opens as SUSPECT. SUSPECT publishes no fault and costs
only a frozen generation estimate; the persistence count
confirmPersistenceCycles = 2 — and this is cycle 2 of 2.
Only now does the classifier run. Persistence, not a higher h,
is this project's answer to R-3's thin margin — the spike's worst
healthy seed peaked at 149.1 ppm against h = 150. A single noise
tail that crosses h is gone on the next sample, because the CUSUM
subtracts k from every one; a stuck damper's residual grows and
clears h on every cycle from the first. It costs one of R-1's
fifteen minutes, where raising h to 8 sigma would cost more
The case stays CONFIRMED/COMPENSATING. Compensation is what
made the residual shrink, so a monitor that cleared the case here
would be talked out of a true diagnosis by the evidence its own
response destroyed — and the damper is still frozen at 0.15.
